source_document: RUO Peptide Program Compliance Standards, v1.1 (August 2026)

attestations.question: Do you ship only within the USA, excluding PO boxes and international addresses?
Do you ship to gyms, med-spas, wellness clinics or weight-loss clinics?
Do first-time orders require an adult signature at 21+?
Does the packing slip carry the RUO disclaimer and research acknowledgement?
Do you maintain a permanent ban list for customers who indicate human use?
Are bans documented and permanent, with no appeal?
Do support staff ever provide dosing, administration or protocol guidance — by email, chat, phone or DM?
What is your standard support response to a dosing question?
Do staff offer to help customers "figure out" protocols?
Do any social accounts contain human-use claims, testimonials or outcome stories?
Do you pay or barter with influencers?
How often are social channels audited, and by whom?
Do you monitor third-party brand mentions and issue cease-and-desist notices?
Is your COA lab independent and accredited? Which accreditation?
How often do you receive new batches, and how quickly are COAs updated?
Do you accept payment through any channel other than card processing?
Do you operate any other storefronts, brands or domains selling the same products?
Do you store the declared research field with every order?
Has any acquirer, processor or platform terminated you?

not_checked.subject: Social media accounts
not_checked.why: Mintro crawls the storefront. It does not follow or read the social media accounts a storefront links to. FDA actively monitors social channels for claims that contradict a seller's own disclaimers, and the standards name off-site marketing as the highest-risk area, so nothing in this report speaks to what those accounts contain.

rules.title: Age affirmation before entry
rules.clause: Every visitor must be stopped at the door and affirm they are 21 or older. This happens before products can be viewed — not at checkout.

rules.title: Products hidden until an account exists
rules.clause: Before shopping for or purchasing any product, a visitor must set up an account, provide the institution they are affiliated with, and electronically acknowledge that everything sold on the site is intended for research use.

rules.title: Guest checkout disabled
rules.clause: There is no anonymous path to purchase. Guest checkout must be turned off entirely.

rules.title: Terms acknowledged at sign-up
rules.clause: The user must actively check “I Agree” against the complete Terms and Conditions. Until they do, account creation cannot proceed.

rules.title: Research field required at sign-up
rules.clause: When the account is established, the buyer must identify their research status. This is a required field — never optional.

rules.title: Research field stored with each order
rules.clause: The selected research field must be stored with every order in your database, not just captured at signup.

params.reason: Order records are server-side. Requires merchant attestation.

rules.title: Terms cover all required clauses
rules.clause: Five points, at minimum: use is restricted to research; human consumption is forbidden; the products play no part in diagnosing, treating or preventing any disease; the buyer indemnifies the seller; and the buyer confirms they are a qualified professional.

rules.title: Footer disclaimer wording
rules.clause: For research and laboratory use only. Not for human or animal consumption.

params.exact: For research and laboratory use only. Not for human or animal consumption.

rules.title: Footer disclaimer is legible
rules.clause: It may not be hidden, shrunk past readability, or tucked inside a collapsed element.

rules.title: Disclaimer on every sampled page
rules.clause: This sentence belongs in the footer of every single page, set in a legible size.

rules.title: CAS number listed
rules.clause: The compound’s exact CAS registry number.

params.note: The check digit is verified, so a phone number, SKU or date range shaped like a registry number is not reported as one. Digits only, so case does not arise.

rules.title: Molecular formula listed
rules.clause: For example, C62H98N16O22 for BPC-157.

params.note: The lookahead requires a digit, so element-symbol-shaped words without subscripts (ATP, DNA, HPLC) no longer read as formulae. Matched case-sensitively: the pattern IS the capitalisation, and forcing the i flag turned it into "three or more letters" (D-135).

rules.title: Molecular weight listed
rules.clause: Expressed in g/mol.

params.note: A number expressed in g/mol, per the clause. Previously satisfied by the label alone, so a page carrying the words "molecular weight" and no figure passed (D-135). Case-insensitive because a page may print G/MOL.

rules.title: Storage conditions listed
rules.clause: For example, “Store at -20°C, desiccated.”

params.note: A storage temperature, per the clause example "Store at -20C, desiccated". Previously satisfied by the label alone, so a page carrying the word "storage" and no condition passed (D-135).

rules.title: No dosing information
rules.clause: Never publish dosing information of any kind: milligram amounts, frequency, route of administration, or injection schedules.

params.note: Mass alone is a legitimate quantity spec. Only co-occurrence with schedule or route is a signal. Human review required — never auto-fail.

rules.title: No pharmaceutical brand names
rules.clause: Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and Rybelsus are off limits, as is every other brand name.

rules.title: No route-of-administration labels
rules.clause: Products cannot be labeled “injectable” or “nasal spray.” These describe how a person would take the product, which makes them administration route claims.

rules.title: No disease or benefit claims
rules.clause: Nothing on the site may state or imply that a compound treats, cures, prevents or diagnoses a disease or condition of any kind.

params.note: High false-positive rate. Review only. 'condition' was removed in D-159: it is a disease word and a legal-boilerplate word, and every storefront's footer carries 'Terms & Conditions'. A real claim about a condition is caught by 'treat' or 'cure' in the same sentence.

rules.title: No links to study databases
rules.clause: Research papers may not be cited or linked, and neither may off-site material of any kind, where doing so would suggest a benefit to a person or point toward human use.

params.note: Reads link hrefs, not prose. A citation named in words rather than linked is not visible to this rule and the title no longer implies otherwise (D-135). Prose claims about human benefit are PROD-008, which scans rendered text.

rules.title: No community abbreviations
rules.clause: Refer to GLP-1 products by chemical name or internal code only — “Semaglutide,” “Tirzepatide.” Never “Sema,” “Tirz,” or similar shorthand.

params.note: Substring of legitimate chemical names. Word-boundary tokenization mandatory. Review only.

rules.title: No therapeutic categories
rules.clause: Products cannot be filed under categories such as “Weight Loss,” “Obesity,” “Longevity,” “Cognitive Enhancement,” “Joint Healing” or “Anti-Aging.”

rules.title: No marketing terms in product names
rules.clause: Names such as “Lean Stack,” “Mass,” “PCT,” “CagriLean,” “Wolverine Peptide” or “Healing Stack” are not permitted.

rules.title: Proper chemical names used
rules.clause: Name each product with the compound’s precise chemical name or its formula — nothing else.

rules.title: No needles or syringes
rules.clause: Offering injection supplies next to peptides is itself evidence of intended injection.

rules.title: No alcohol wipes
rules.clause: Their obvious purpose is preparing an injection site, which places the sale in a human-injection context.

rules.title: No HCG or HGH
rules.clause: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin and Human Growth Hormone both require prescriptions.

params.note: Product URLs only. These terms appear routinely in research writing; matching editorial content would auto-fail a merchant for publishing, not selling. See D-010.

rules.title: No tablets or pills
rules.clause: Oral dosage forms are not permitted.

params.note: Covers tablets and pills only. Capsule labelling is CATG-006.

rules.title: Reconstitution solution labelling
rules.clause: Bacteriostatic water is permitted when it carries the label “Reconstitution Solution for Laboratory Use.” Keep injection language off the listing, and attach no pharmaceutical brand names such as Pfizer or Hospira.

rules.title: Capsule labelling
rules.clause: Capsules may be sold only where they are exclusively for research use and properly labeled, listed with chemical names and CAS numbers only. Anything short of that is prohibited.

rules.title: Non-peptide research compounds in the catalogue
rules.clause: The catalogue offered under a research peptide programme may contain compounds that are not peptides. This rule reports which of them are present and names them.

params.note: Compound names and synonyms are taken from USADA’s published SARM guidance, which accompanies the WADA Prohibited List (S1.2, Other Anabolic Agents) — a specimen, not recollection (D-118). That source names eight SARMs and separately names five compounds "also sometimes marketed as SARMs": SR9009, SR9011, ibutamoren (MK-677), GW501516 (cardarine) and YK-11. Both groups are listed here because the rule reports non-peptide compounds, not SARMs; a rule titled for SARMs would misname four of the seven families seen in the first catalogue crawled. The source is authoritative for naming and for the SARM boundary. It is not a definition of the programme’s scope, because nothing published is — the programme document does not mention non-peptides at all.

rules.title: COA linked on each sampled product page
rules.clause: Each product page must link to the COA for the current batch, issued by an accredited independent third-party testing laboratory.

rules.title: Certificate reports a test date within 60 days
rules.clause: Refresh COAs at least every 60 days. When a new batch arrives, update immediately rather than waiting for the cycle.

rules.title: Certificate states purity at or above 98%
rules.clause: A minimum of 98% purity for all products, and every purity figure must be backed by a Certificate of Analysis.

rules.title: COA contains all required fields
rules.clause: The COA must identify the batch or lot number, the testing date, the compound identity, the purity percentage, and the method used (HPLC preferred).

rules.title: Lab is accredited and independent
rules.clause: Each product page must link to the COA for the current batch, issued by an accredited independent third-party testing laboratory.

params.reason: Accreditation and authenticity cannot be verified from a PDF. Forged COAs are a known failure mode. Independent assay is the only real control.

rules.title: Certificate links serve a readable certificate
rules.clause: Each product page must link to the COA for the current batch, issued by an accredited independent third-party testing laboratory.

params.note: That the certificates cannot be read is an observation in its own right, not merely the reason three other checks are unevaluated: nothing they state is verifiable by anyone following the link. review_only because a link serving the wrong asset is the kind of thing a human should confirm before it counts against a merchant (D-136).

rules.title: Shipping policy states USA only
rules.clause: Domestic addresses only. No PO boxes, and nothing crossing the border.

rules.title: No PO boxes
rules.clause: Domestic addresses only. No PO boxes, and nothing crossing the border.

params.reason: Establishing this requires entering a PO box address at checkout and seeing whether the merchant accepts it, which means submitting data to a live store. The crawl submits nothing. Requires merchant attestation.

rules.title: Adult signature on first orders
rules.clause: Every first-time customer order must require an adult signature on delivery, with 21+ confirmed.

rules.title: Packing slip disclaimers
rules.clause: Include the research-use-only disclaimer and the research-professional acknowledgement in the shipment itself.

params.reason: Physical document. Requires a test order or merchant attestation.

rules.title: Ban list maintained
rules.clause: Keep a live ban list. A customer who so much as hints at human consumption is removed for good, with no appeal, and the reason is written down.

rules.title: No affiliate or referral program URLs
rules.clause: Do not operate an affiliate or referral program.

params.note: Scope widened from pages to content (D-024). scope pages matched zero URLs on every storefront scanned, leaving this critical auto_fail rule blind.

rules.title: No testimonials or outcome stories
rules.clause: Do not post testimonials, before-and-after photos, recovery stories, or user reviews that describe health outcomes.

params.note: Located by review markup a plugin emits for search engines, not by a class name the theme chose (D-159). The old selector [class*=review] matched 'preview' and missed any theme naming its section differently. A testimonial written as plain prose with no markup is not detected, and the finding says so.

rules.title: Social accounts linked from the storefront
rules.clause: From social profiles and posts, link to the site’s home page and nowhere deeper.

params.note: Bio-link inspection requires platform fetch. Best-effort.

rules.title: Social post content
rules.clause: Whatever the channel, a post lives under the product-page rules — naming, claims, categories and disclaimers all carry over.

params.reason: Post-level review needs platform API access or a commercial listening tool. Not covered.

rules.title: Monthly social audits
rules.clause: Sweep every channel at least once a month, and act on any post found carrying human-use language.

rules.title: Affiliate program linked from the homepage
rules.clause: Do not operate an affiliate or referral program.

params.note: Companion to OFFS-001, which matches affiliate URLs. A merchant whose affiliate links carry no distinguishing URL — swisschems.is links 'Affiliate Program' to / — is invisible to any url_pattern rule. Link text is weaker evidence than a dedicated URL and a nav label can be incidental, so this is permanently review_only. See D-027.

rules.title: Editorial content on therapeutic topics
rules.clause: Nothing on the site may state or imply that a compound treats, cures, prevents or diagnoses a disease or condition of any kind.

params.note: A slug indicates topic, not claim. Only a human reading the article can tell rigorous chemistry from a dosing guide, so this rule surfaces candidates and never renders a verdict. Permanently review_only — see D-020.

rules.title: No peer-to-peer payment methods named on public pages
rules.clause: To an investigator, a seller collecting through Venmo, Cash App, Zelle or PayPal Friends & Family looks like one sidestepping the fraud controls that come with a standard merchant account.

rules.title: Card processing through a merchant account
rules.clause: Card payments must run through a legitimate merchant processor that performs proper KYC. How a seller collects money is read as evidence of how the business is run.

params.reason: Identifying the processor requires reaching checkout, which a merchant who correctly gates it never shows an anonymous visitor. Payment marks in a footer name a card network, not the processor behind it. Requires merchant attestation.

rules.title: Refund and chargeback policy published
rules.clause: Publish a refund and chargeback policy, clearly written and easy to find.

rules.title: FAQ free of dosing or administration advice
rules.clause: No dosing advice, no administration guidance, and nothing a reader could take as instruction for using a drug — in any channel, by any staff member.

rules.title: Support channels free of human-use language
rules.clause: This standard covers every channel — your FAQ and site copy, email, live chat, phone, and social media direct messages.

params.reason: Not reachable by crawl. Sampled transcript review or mystery shopping only.

rules.title: Staff do not help with protocols
rules.clause: Staff must never offer to help a customer “figure out” a protocol.
